headline: Unbeaten Santa Clara host Benfica — and the market favours the visitors
summary: Santa Clara have not lost in 8 league games and sit fourth, one point behind Benfica, so a win on Monday would put them above them. But Benfica are clear favourites: 67.4% to win, more than six times Santa Clara's 11.2% chance. Benfica create chances worth 2.07 goals a game and arrive 11 days after a 4-1 win over Celtic, and over 2.5 goals is a 51.1% chance. Santa Clara get a 1.25-goal head start on the handicap — the market expects a Benfica win, not a rout.
read: Santa Clara are unbeaten in the league and sit one point behind Benfica, but the market still makes Benfica 67.4% favourites and rates them about 1.3 goals the better side. Benfica arrive off a 4-1 Europa League win with eleven days' rest and a coach openly planning around this trip, while Santa Clara's resistance has come from a defence conceding under half an expected goal per game.

facts.fact: Benfica are 67.4% favourites to win at Santa Clara, more than six times the home side's 11.2% chance.
facts.meaning: The market expects Benfica to take the points, but the handicap price says it does not expect a rout.

facts.fact: Santa Clara are fourth on 18 points, one behind Benfica's 19, and a win would put them above Benfica.
facts.meaning: This is a meeting of two of the league's best starters, not a mismatch on paper.

facts.fact: Santa Clara are unbeaten in the league: five wins and three draws in eight games, form WDWWD.
facts.meaning: They arrive on a run of results, with a full week's rest behind them.

facts.fact: Santa Clara's only defeat in their last five was 2-3 at Mafra in the Taça de Portugal on 18 October.
facts.meaning: The one blot on their recent record, and a reminder that they can be opened up.

facts.fact: Benfica average 2.07 xG per game over their last five; Santa Clara average 1.15.
facts.meaning: Benfica create roughly twice as much, which is the football basis for their price.

facts.fact: The market rates Benfica about 1.3 goals better than Santa Clara, with the fair handicap line at 1.31.
facts.meaning: Benfica need to win by two clear goals to fully cover the -1.25 line; a one-goal win only half-pays.

facts.fact: The market's goals line sits at 2.55, with Over 2.5 at 51.1%.
facts.meaning: Three goals or more is roughly a coin flip — this is not priced as a goalfest.

facts.fact: Benfica's last match was a 4-1 Europa League win over Celtic on 15 October, 11 days before this game.
facts.meaning: A fully rested Benfica, and O Jogo reports Marco Silva is set to rotate for the Omonia tie with Monday's trip to Santa Clara in mind.

sources.fact: Santa Clara are unbeaten and have the best defence in the Liga going into the Benfica match, according to A Bola.
Santa Clara will not drop in the table even if they lose to Benfica, and would overtake Benfica in the standings if they win, A Bola reports.
A Bola describes Santa Clara as under no pressure for the visit of Benfica.
Jhon Durán has a right-knee problem and did not travel to Cyprus for the Omonia game, with the expectation he will be back for Monday's trip to Santa Clara.
OneFootball reports Durán is training and his knee problem is not considered serious, but he is unlikely to be fully fit for the Omonia tie before the Santa Clara match.
Marco Silva is set to rotate his Benfica eleven for the Omonia game with Monday's visit to Santa Clara in mind, O Jogo reports.
Benfica travelled to Cyprus with five absences, forcing Marco Silva to call on B-team players, according to A Bola.
Benfica sit second in the Liga on 19 points heading into the Santa Clara match.
